applied.change: Compared every file in ref_arch/new/ by sha256 before touching anything: 14 byte-identical, 1 differing, 1 new. Copied the two up, re-verified each by hash after the copy, deleted the fourteen identical copies only after asserting equality a second time, and removed the empty directory. Reference Model.dc.html's diff was cosmetic -- reformatting plus a nav link to the stack -- and extract_reference_model.py --check still holds 14 of 14 with 40 cards, so nothing downstream moved.

Recorded rather than resolved, because the missing document is the owner's to supply. The derived JSON carries the claim verbatim in a `source_claimed` field so the dangling reference is visible in the artifact itself rather than only in a comment, and STATUS row 89 states the condition: every stack claim cites a fetched record or is marked proposed. Nothing in the repo cites the stack as sourced evidence yet.

Declared KEY_ALIAS = {'cross': 'concerns'} in the extractor with the reason in a comment, echoed it into the derived JSON as `key_aliases`, and added a check that prints which aliases are actually in use on every run. The join check resolves through the alias, so a future key that does NOT resolve still fails.

Wrote a small recursive-descent reader for the JS literal subset the source uses -- objects, arrays, single-quoted strings with backslash escapes, booleans, null, integers, bare keys, and the file's own T() helper mapped onto its seven positional fields -- instead of reusing split_args(). The reason is in the module docstring so the next author does not 'simplify' it back. Its first run caught a real bug in my own key handling: obj() tested whether a key was quoted AFTER consuming it, so self.i had already moved and it double-advanced past the colon.

verification: 11 of 11 extractor checks hold; output is idempotent (--check green immediately after a write). Proven able to fail in both directions before being wired: a hand-edited licence in the JSON gives real exit 1 with 'differs from what the source renders'; a source that names a tool not in the catalogue gives 'FAIL every tool a port names exists in tools: [NoSuchTool]'. Restored, real exit 0. Wired into tools/phase.py as the blocking `ref stack` gate, 23 gates to 24.
